rule: Never judge a visual change by reasoning about the code. Run `npm run shots` and LOOK at docs/shots/<label>/, comparing against docs/shots/00-baseline/. Never ask the user what something looks like.
reason: This project exists as a web port for exactly one reason: in the Godot original the agent could not see rendered output, so every art pass round-tripped through a human reviewer and the visual bar in sprite_style_guide.md was never met. The harness removes that bottleneck. Reintroducing the human-as-eyeball loop wastes the entire reason the port exists.
triggering_incident: sprite_style_guide.md line 207 states outright: 'The developer (user) serves as the visual reviewer since the AI cannot see the rendered result.' Milestone 1 of BRIEF.md was built specifically to retire that sentence.
enforced_by: npm run shots (byte-identical across runs; any pixel diff vs baseline is a real change)
retrieval_hints: how do I check what the game looks like

rule: Skin shadows must use SHADOW_SKIN (rosy, hue 0.98); everything else uses SHADOW_COOL (blue-violet, 0.65). Hue interpolation always takes the short way around the circle. Never add a colour literal outside src/art/palette.ts, and give every migrated sprite a declared palette so bake() can snap to it.
reason: Pushing skin's 27-degree hue toward blue-violet travels through yellow-green, so the shaded half of a face comes out olive - the single most damaging artefact on a character sprite. The style guide asks for red-brown on skin specifically for this reason. Separately, derived shades, cast shadows and the outline blend each mint a new colour per application: Maren measured 57 distinct colours on one 32x32 sprite before snapping, which is what makes a cast stop reading as one piece of art.
triggering_incident: Milestone 2: Maren's face rendered olive on the shaded side twice - first from the linear hue lerp, then again from nearest-colour snapping sending a deep cool-brown cast shadow onto a dark green palette entry.
enforced_by: node tools/focus.mjs <key> then compare lit vs shaded skin hue: shaded must move toward red (lower hue), never toward green
